summary.headline: Shilchar Q2 FY27 revenue rose 43% QoQ to INR192.61 crore with EBITDA margin at 20.8%, while FY27 INR750 crore target is reiterated.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR192.61 crore, up 43% QoQ and 12% YoY, as deferred Q1 export dispatches landed and domestic demand stayed strong. EBITDA excluding other income was INR40.06 crore (20.8% margin, up from 16.4% in Q1) and PAT was INR32.98 crore (16.5% margin). Management reiterated the FY27 revenue target of INR750 crore, with H1 sales of about INR330 crore and an order book of over INR550 crore. Margins remain below the roughly 28-30% levels of FY24-FY26, and management shifted guidance to absolute EBITDA (INR200-250 crore) rather than percentage margin.

financial_highlights.metric: Net working capital increase in H1
financial_highlights.change: includes financial assets up to about INR29 crore, per analyst

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Export mix was about 40% in Q2 and the order book is about 60:40 domestic:export. Middle East shipments were still below normal, offset partly by North America, where US tariffs were withdrawn in February. Management said export margins are higher than domestic, but did not quantify.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic demand was described as very strong throughout. Mix is mainly renewable-related transformers, with distribution transformers made in very small quantities.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR750 crore reiterated; management said it will be more than that, and analysts were told quarterly run-rate of INR225-230 crore is needed.
FY27 EBITDA target is more than INR200 crore (INR225-250 crore in absolute terms) with percentage margin unspecified; management would not give a margin number and said it is difficult to guess.
Margins expected to improve in Q3 and Q4 with about 100% capacity utilisation and more export orders.
FY28 revenue target about INR1,000 crore; FY29 target INR1,250-1,500 crore, with maximum INR1,500 crore at 100% utilisation of 14,000 MVA capacity.
Management said margins may fall as capacity grows, but targets absolute EBITDA growth; the same or higher EBITDA margin is targeted in the long term.
capex_capacity: Expansion Phase 3 adds 6,500 MVA, taking total capacity to 14,000 MVA; commissioning expected April 2027.
Civil foundation, PEB erection and utility work are in progress; all major production equipment has been ordered.
Current utilisation is about 80% of installed capacity in Q2; management expects about 100% in Q3 and Q4 FY27.
Approvals for 220 kV class transformers expected 3-6 months after the new plant starts; existing customers have given verbal commitments for orders.
Management said breakeven utilisation on the new capacity is about 35-40%.
demand_pricing: Lead times: about 3-6 months for lower kV classes; more than 1 year for higher kV classes.
Raw material prices have stabilised but remain above pre-crisis levels; new orders are priced on current raw material costs. Management said the price rise was partly passed on, but not fully.
Working capital: no bank working-capital borrowing; receivables are mainly LC-backed (for example, 180-day LCs with interest borne by the customer).
Demand drivers cited: data centres, renewables, BESS, transmission and distribution. Management said capacity additions should not pressure margins for at least a couple of years.
Analyst cited raw material cost at about 71-72% of sales versus about 60% earlier; management did not dispute this.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q2 revenue jump came from deferred Q1 revenue, and what is the FY27 path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said part of Q2 came from Q1 deferrals and part from new orders. It said H2 quarterly sales should be INR225-230 crore to reach the INR750 crore target.

qa_highlights.question: How much did higher freight cut EBITDA, and can margins return to about 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: No quantification of freight impact was given. Management said margins will fall as volumes rise, but absolute EBITDA is targeted at INR225-250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Are approvals in place for 220 kV transformers?
qa_highlights.answer: No approvals yet; applications follow plant commissioning, expected to take 3-6 months. Margins on 220 kV are expected to match current classes.

qa_highlights.question: Are there sustained margin outlooks (for example 23-25%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a percentage. It said it is focused on absolute EBITDA; one analyst's implied 23-24% margin was framed as 'we will be trying for that'.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakeven utilisation on the new capacity, and what is the demand risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 35-40% utilisation is breakeven and that demand is supported by power demand growth. It acknowledged a trade-off between growth and margin.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any acquisition or diversification plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is exploring options but is bound by an NDA and will disclose once progressed.

risks_watch: Middle East shipping and logistics costs remain high, and export volumes to the region are not normal yet.
Raw material costs are above pre-crisis levels; management says they will not fully normalise. Pass-through is only partial.
FY27 EBITDA target of INR200 crore needs about 30% margin in H2 on the management's own assumptions, while Q2 margin was 20.8%.
Heavy capacity additions industry-wide and competition from new entrants, including Waaree, may pressure pricing.
Watch for 220 kV approvals after April 2027 commissioning, Q3 revenue run-rate of INR225 crore, and the export mix improving from 40%.
Working capital rose sharply in H1, with receivables and financial assets up; management attributes this to LC-backed terms.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the order book, but evasive on margin percentages, freight impact and export mix, and cautious on raw material outlook. Management repeatedly moved the discussion to absolute EBITDA and the INR750 crore revenue target.
key_quotes: So with 30% EBITDA, if we have done INR200 crores, maybe the EBITDA margin will come down, but our EBITDA in value terms will be maybe INR225 crores, INR250 crores.
I don't think that it will completely stabilize till all the Middle East crisis and other things gets concluded.
Only, I think 35%, 40% utilization of the capacity will be a breakeven for us and that is...

adds.what: Expansion Phase 3 adds 6,500 MVA, taking total capacity to 14,000 MVA

growth.why: FY27 revenue target of INR750 cr reiterated (about 31% over FY26-implied base is not stated; H1 about INR330 cr, order book over INR550 cr), backed by Phase 3 adding 6,500 MVA (commissioning April 2027) and utilisation rising from about 80% toward 100% in Q3-Q4.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Margin rose to 20.8% in Q2 from 16.4% in Q1 and management expects improvement in Q3-Q4 at about 100% utilisation, but it declined to give a margin percentage and remains well below the 28-30% of FY24-FY26, with raw material at about 71-72% of sales.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Phase 3 adds 6,500 MVA taking capacity to 14,000 MVA; civil, PEB and utility work are in progress and all major production equipment is already ordered, with commissioning set for April 2027.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Utilisation is about 80% in Q2 and management expects about 100% in Q3-Q4, with H2 quarterly sales needed at INR225-230 crore to reach the INR750 crore FY27 target against H1 of about INR330 crore, and an order book above INR550 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 80% and will reach about 100% in Q3-Q4 FY27, and Phase 3 is already committed, so further capacity beyond 14,000 MVA is needed to reach the FY29 INR1,250-1,500 crore target (management cites 100% utilisation of 14,000 MVA as the cap at INR1,500 crore).

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said FY27 revenue will be more than INR750 crore, but the H2 run-rate needed (INR225-230 crore per quarter) is a step-up from Q2 revenue of INR192.61 crore and depends on the Middle East recovering.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA target of INR200-250 crore needs about 30% margin in H2 per the brief, against Q2 margin of 20.8%, with raw material at about 71-72% of sales and Middle East freight and export volumes still below normal.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: 220 kV class transformers are planned, with approvals expected 3-6 months after the new plant starts and existing customers already giving verbal order commitments.

rows.label: Order book above INR550 crore, 60:40 domestic:export
rows.why: Order book is over INR550 crore, backing the H2 revenue ramp, with lead times of 3-6 months for lower kV and more than 1 year for higher kV classes.

rows.label: H1 working capital build of about INR200 crore
rows.why: Net working capital rose about INR200 crore in H1 with receivables mostly LC-backed on 180-day terms and no bank working-capital borrowing, so cash conversion stays a watch item as revenue ramps.

rows.label: North America export recovery after US tariff withdrawal
rows.why: US tariffs were withdrawn in February and North America is offsetting weak Middle East shipments, but export mix is about 40% and management did not quantify export margin uplift.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the order book and the INR750 crore revenue target, but declined to give margin percentages and did not quantify freight or export mix; analysts pressed on the implied margin needed for the EBITDA target, raw material cost pass-through and 220 kV approvals.
